title: Discount Stacking: A Denial and an Approval Across a Rule Change
scenario_text:
A deal desk analyst at Selwyn Media must decide whether two discounts can be stacked on a renewal, given two prior decisions and a mid-year rule change.

**Decision A (2024-01)**
Customer 'Ashford Media' | 2-year renewal | total contract value (TCV) $600K. Requested to stack the 15% loyalty discount with the 10% volume discount. Deal Desk DENIED. Note: 'Stacking requires TCV of at least $1M; Ashford is $600K. Only one discount may apply.'

**Decision B (2024-04)**
Customer 'Brindley Group' | 3-year renewal | TCV $700K. Requested the same stacking. Deal Desk APPROVED. Note: 'Under the new rule effective 2024-03-01, renewals of 3 years or longer auto-qualify for stacking regardless of TCV.'

**Current request C (2024-09-16)**
Customer 'Caldicott Press' | 3-year renewal | TCV $650K. Requesting to stack the 15% loyalty and 10% volume discounts.

**Discount Stacking Policy (current, effective 2024-03-01)**
The 15% loyalty discount may stack with the 10% volume discount only when TCV is at least $1M, EXCEPT that renewals with a term of 3 years or longer auto-qualify for stacking regardless of TCV.

**Slack — #deal-desk**
AE: 'We denied stacking on a sub-$1M renewal back in January — Ashford at $600K. Caldicott is $650K, also under $1M, so we deny, right?'
Analyst: 'January was a 2-year deal, and it was before the March stacking rule. Caldicott is a 3-year renewal — let me check which precedent actually fits.'
question: How should the analyst handle Caldicott Press's stacking request?
choices: Deny stacking, consistent with the January denial of stacking on a similar sub-$1M renewal.

Approve stacking: as a 3-year renewal, Caldicott auto-qualifies under the March 1, 2024 rule regardless of TCV — matching the April approval — and the January 2-year denial predates that rule, so it does not govern.
Approve stacking only if Caldicott raises its TCV above $1M; otherwise apply just one discount.
Escalate to the VP of Sales because the January denial and the April approval appear to conflict.
